instruction: Find and highlight the cell corresponding to the peak Food Bill cost in the 2020 data section.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding max Food Bill in 2020 data. Verified with data: 2020 Food Bills (rows 20-31, column G) are [120, 125, 110, 130, 160, 130, 130, 130, 110, 115, 125, 125]. Maximum is 160 at May (row 24, cell G24). The evaluator checks if cell G24 has highlighting applied.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts cell fill information from cell G24 using openpyxl
Metric correctly checks if the cell has highlighting applied by comparing result.has_fill with expected.has_fill
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) to ensure highlighting is persisted for verification
Expected value (has_fill: true) semantically matches the instruction requirement to apply highlighting
Data flow is correct: getter extracts fill state from G24 -> metric compares has_fill boolean -> returns 1.0 if highlighted
The static warning about parameter type mismatch is a false positive - the metric function correctly handles expected as the rules dict when type='rule'
Evaluator verifies the cell is highlighted but assumes user identified the correct cell (G24) - this is acceptable because highlighting wrong cell would fail verification
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a secondary check to verify that cell G24 contains the maximum value (160) to ensure the user identified the correct cell, though current approach is acceptable

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_cell_highlighted__d16b79868b1b27e16371419147c94ae4 second parameter type (dict) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
